papers.subject: Erdős #249
papers.question: What is the exact rank of the totient kernel at every integer base, which parts are formalised, and why does Erdős #249 remain open?
papers.precis: For every integer base k≥2, including composite bases, the totient kernel through level e≥1 has an explicit rational basis of size k^e + 1; level 0 has dimension 1. The paper gives an ordinary proof using arithmetic independence. Lean also proves all-base canonical-family independence and the complete rank unconditionally by CRT and Dirichlet. No t = 83 certificate or cofinal certificate supply is proved; Erdős #249 remains open.

papers.subject: Erdős #251
papers.question: What tail-shift condition would prove irrationality in Erdős #251, which natural affine schedules provably cannot supply it, and what prime-gap input still survives?
papers.precis: The paper identifies the complete prime-gap tails and classifies rationality by integrality of their shifts. Two adjacent shifts in (-1,1) with unequal associated gaps cannot both be integral, so their cofinal occurrence for every positive shift would prove irrationality. These countermodels delimit growth, parity, congruence, and local-statistics arguments; the prime-specific cofinal small-shift assertion remains open.

papers.subject: Erdős #257
papers.question: Which Mersenne-support subseries are settled, what finite-period and achievement-set structure is proved, and what still blocks Erdős #257?
papers.precis: Fix a finite nonempty prime set P and put h(a)=∏_{p∈P}p^{v_p(a)}. If an infinite support A has ∑_{a∈A}h(a)/(a(2^{h(a)}−1)) finite, its reciprocal Mersenne subseries is irrational at every integer base b≥2, as is the subseries on every infinite subset of A. The paper prints a complete ordinary proof and a host with divergent reciprocal sum, so the criterion is strictly weaker than reciprocal summability. A common observation window also proves hereditary irrationality for unions of weighted supports and strengthened positive-cover supports. These are ordinary results, not Lean theorems, and no priority claim is made. Universal Erdős #257 remains open.

It also proves that distinct concyclic zeros in degree n≥3 admit an adjacent chord shorter than 2 in {|f|<1} when their circle radius ρ satisfies 2ρ^n≤1; this alternation proof is not formalised in Lean. For squarefree monic polynomials, if the least critical-value modulus μ is at most 13/25, there is also such a connector. Without a root-location restriction, the scaled result gives a path shorter than (5/2) μ^(1/n) in {|f|<(25/13)μ}. Separate length-area and critical-value estimates give further control. Exact counterexamples show why these ingredients do not yield the unrestricted connector theorem; Erdős #1041 remains open.

papers.title: Irrationality of F(31/4) and the Exact Normalized Hankel Order
papers.subject: Erdős #1049
papers.question: For Erdős #1049, which Lambert values at rational bases are proved irrational, what exact Hankel invariant does it compute, and why does the method still miss 3/2?
papers.precis: Specialising Zudilin's 2004 construction to rational bases, the paper proves F(a/b) irrational for coprime integers a>b≥1 when log b / log a is below the explicit threshold (approximately 0.40568, the reciprocal of Zudilin's exponent bound); in particular F((31/4)^r) is irrational for every positive integer r, with a uniform irrationality-exponent bound. The specialisation and its estimates are an ordinary proof; Lean checks finite subclaims. A second construction shows that Zudilin's lower bound for the normalised Hankel order is attained and computes the leading coefficient. The criterion does not cover 3/2, where a primitive noncollapsed kernel and analytic remainder control are still needed.
papers.owns: the problem-specific exposition for Erdős #1049: the ordinary rational-base irrationality theorem and uniform exponent bound for the (31/4)^r family, the exact normalised Hankel order and leading coefficient, the content and endpoint obstructions, and the remaining approximant and remainder construction at 3/2

papers.title: From a Cold Clone to a Proof Receipt
papers.subject: Systems paper
papers.question: How can a reasoning agent comprehend a large Lean corpus before compiling, then cross into replayable proof authority and incremental validation?
papers.precis: A large formal library can be mechanically exact and still be practically unreadable to the next reader or reasoning agent. At the audited revision a cold clone exposes a bounded six-line tour over 1,019 Lean modules and 153,238 declarations, a map of ten programmes, 101 curated claims, and an elaborated reference graph, none of which requires a build. 503 of those modules and 8,171 of those declarations are marked machine-generated certificate shards, counted as source and never as claims, and that marking is a classification floor rather than the true generated share, since earlier emitted families predate the markers. Navigation receives no proof authority: probe verdicts come from the pinned Lean process and cannot be authored by the agent, and a claim must cite an accepted probe that replay reruns from stored bytes. The audit was author-operated; no external contributor had completed the tour or documented return path by 31 August 2026.
papers.owns: the agent-navigation architecture: layered corpus projections, bounded intent routing, kernel-authored session receipts, focused builds, and exact dependency-index cache receipts

papers.title: From Spare Compute to Cumulative Mathematics
papers.subject: Systems paper
papers.question: How can outsiders contribute compute, mathematical direction, architecture, or review without receiving authority to declare a proof?
papers.precis: A public Lean repository can serve as a shared conversion layer between compute, agent capability, human mathematical direction, infrastructure quality, and review. The paper defines role-bounded work packets, two first-class contribution tracks, provenance and credit, safe untrusted returns, and a candidate-to-attention funnel. Formal verification strengthens one evidence layer; human meaning, novelty, significance, and broad mathematical adoption remain separate. The eight Erdős problems are hard test worlds and all remain open. This is a working prototype; no completed external cold clone or landed outside contribution was recorded by 31 August 2026.
papers.owns: the open-source strategy: how outside compute, mathematics, architecture improvements, review, and credit enter one bounded commons

papers.title: Plectis: What a Stranger Can Check
papers.subject: Systems paper
papers.question: What may a stranger conclude from public evidence when the author chose both what to publish and what counts as a pass?
papers.precis: The author publishes selected code, fixed inputs, expected results, decision rules, and run records while the larger system stays private. What can a stranger conclude after rerunning them? A matching result shows repeatability for one stated public case. It does not establish where the code came from, whether the expected answer is correct, whether the published selection resembles the private whole, or whether the private system works reliably. The contribution is a method for making one selected disagreement local, not a score.
papers.owns: the evidence boundary: what a passing public run does and does not establish
